# Figures: Decisions

<!-- Generated by `npm run figures:docs` from src/components/figures/catalog.ts. Edit the catalogue, then run it again. -->

What did I decide, on what evidence? The reasoning made visible: the hypothesis before the data, what was traded for what, what is known and what is guessed, how it ended.

How to add one to an entry, and the rules they all follow: [figures.md](../figures.md).

In this file: [Hypothesis](#hypothesis) · [JobStory](#jobstory) · [Matrix](#matrix) · [Tradeoffs](#tradeoffs) · [ScopeCut](#scopecut) · [Claims](#claims) · [Quote](#quote) · [Verdict](#verdict)

## Hypothesis

`J-01` · If, then, because: a hypothesis set so it can fail, with the metric and the rule that decide it.

**Use it for**

- Experiment, "Context" or "How I measured": written before looking at the result.
- Review and comparison, "What I would test": one figure per hypothesis.

**Skills Map:** territories measurement, activation, discovery; skills `hypotheses`, `experiment-guardrails`, `assumption-mapping`, `activation-experiments`, `deciding-under-uncertainty`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`if`** *(required)* `string`: The change.
- **`then`** *(required)* `string`: The expected effect on a number.
- **`because`** *(required)* `string`: The reason it should work.
- **`metric`** `string`: The one number that decides it.
- **`keepIf`** `string`: The result that means keep, agreed before the data.
- **`stopIf`** `string`: The result that means stop or revert.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Hypothesis
  if="new learners can start a lesson before creating an account"
  then="more of them finish a first lesson"
  because="they get something back before they are asked for anything."
  metric="New visitors who finish a first lesson within 24 hours"
  keepIf="The interval for the difference is above zero"
  stopIf="Accounts per visitor fall by more than a tenth"
/>
```

## JobStory

`J-02` · When, I want to, so I can: the job a product is hired for.

**Use it for**

- Review and comparison, "Who it is for" and "The shared job".
- Case study, "Context": the user and the progress they were after.

**Skills Map:** territories discovery, strategy; skills `jobs-to-be-done`, `user-motivations`, `context-of-use`, `problem-statements`, `value-proposition`, `target-audience`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`when`** *(required)* `string`: The situation.
- **`want`** *(required)* `string`: What the person wants to do.
- **`so`** *(required)* `string`: The progress they are after.
- **`who`** `string`: Who says it, when it is one segment.
- **`today`** `string`: What they use today instead.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<JobStory
  when="I am responsible for more than the code"
  want="see what I am missing"
  so="apply it to the product problem in front of me."
  who="Experienced engineer with a live product or a side project"
  today="Their own unstructured practice"
/>
```

## Matrix

`J-03` · A two-by-two with numbered points and the list beside it.

**Use it for**

- Case study, "Decisions": options placed by impact and effort.
- Before an experiment: assumptions placed by importance and evidence, to choose which to test.

**Not for:** Positions you cannot defend. If the placement is a feeling, say so in the caption or use a list.

**Skills Map:** territories strategy, discovery, cross-cutting; skills `impact-effort`, `opportunity-assessment`, `assumption-mapping`, `evidence-strength`, `product-risk`, `problem-severity`, `sequencing`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`x`** *(required)* `{ label: string; low?: string; high?: string }`: The horizontal axis and the words at its ends.
- **`y`** *(required)* `{ label: string; low?: string; high?: string }`: The vertical axis.
- **`items`** *(required)* `{ label: string; x: number; y: number; note?: string; pick?: boolean }[]`: `x` and `y` run from 0 (low) to 1 (high). `pick` marks the one chosen.
- **`quadrants`** `[string, string, string, string]`: Names for top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right.
- **`focus`** `'tl' | 'tr' | 'bl' | 'br'`: The quadrant to tint: where you want things to be.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example: Impact against effort**

```mdx
<Matrix
  title="Five ways to get more people through the first lesson"
  x={{ label: 'Effort', low: 'Days', high: 'Months' }}
  y={{ label: 'Expected effect', low: 'Small', high: 'Large' }}
  quadrants={['Do first', 'Plan', 'Fill in', 'Leave']}
  focus="tl"
  items={[
    { label: 'Lesson before account', x: 0.2, y: 0.85, pick: true, note: 'Removes three decisions' },
    { label: 'Shorter level test', x: 0.36, y: 0.58 },
    { label: 'Social sign-in', x: 0.3, y: 0.28 },
    { label: 'New lesson engine', x: 0.85, y: 0.78 },
    { label: 'Welcome video', x: 0.62, y: 0.18 },
  ]}
  caption="Placed by judgment, before any data. The experiment tests the one in pink."
  evidence="assumed"
/>
```

**Example: Assumptions: importance against evidence**

```mdx
<Matrix
  x={{ label: 'Evidence', low: 'None', high: 'Strong' }}
  y={{ label: 'What rests on it', low: 'Little', high: 'Everything' }}
  quadrants={['Test first', 'Keep watching', 'Park', 'Known']}
  focus="tl"
  items={[
    { label: 'Engineers want a map of the discipline', x: 0.15, y: 0.9, pick: true },
    { label: 'A weekly review brings people back', x: 0.2, y: 0.62 },
    { label: 'LinkedIn reaches them', x: 0.4, y: 0.45 },
    { label: 'The Skills Map loads fast enough', x: 0.9, y: 0.3 },
  ]}
  evidence="assumed"
/>
```

## Tradeoffs

`J-04` · Positions between two goods: where a product sits, or where a change moved it.

**Use it for**

- Review and experiment, "Trade-offs": what was chosen and what it cost.
- Comparison, "Where they differ", with `was` as the other product.

**Not for:** A good thing against a bad thing. Both ends must be worth having, or it is not a trade-off.

**Skills Map:** territories cross-cutting, strategy, engineering; skills `tradeoffs`, `technical-tradeoffs`, `opportunity-cost`, `differentiation`, `competitive-advantage`, `balancing-signals`, `second-order-effects`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`items`** *(required)* `{ left: string; right: string; at: number; was?: number; note?: string }[]`: `at` runs from 0 (all left) to 1 (all right). `was` draws a second marker and the move between them.
- **`names`** `{ at?: string; was?: string }`: Names for the two markers when `was` is used.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Tradeoffs
  title="What lesson-first trades away"
  names={{ at: 'Lesson first', was: 'Account first' }}
  items={[
    {
      left: 'Value before effort',
      right: 'An account from the start',
      at: 0.18,
      was: 0.86,
      note: 'Fewer accounts on day one, more people who finish a lesson.',
    },
    {
      left: 'One path for everyone',
      right: 'Lessons matched to level',
      at: 0.3,
      was: 0.72,
      note: 'The level test moves to after the first lesson.',
    },
    {
      left: 'Simple to build',
      right: 'Progress never lost',
      at: 0.38,
      note: 'Guest progress lives in the browser until sign-up.',
    },
  ]}
/>
```

## ScopeCut

`J-05` · What is in, what was cut and what waits, in columns.

**Use it for**

- Experiment and improvement, "What I built" and "What I shipped": the smallest version worth learning from.
- Review and comparison, "Scope": what I looked at and what I left out.

**Skills Map:** territories strategy, shipping, cross-cutting; skills `scope-cutting`, `mvp`, `smallest-valuable-increment`, `vertical-slicing`, `small-batches`, `challenging-requirements`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`kept`** *(required)* `(string | { text: string; note?: string })[]`: What is in.
- **`cut`** *(required)* `(string | { text: string; note?: string })[]`: What was left out on purpose.
- **`later`** `(string | { text: string; note?: string })[]`: What waits for the result.
- **`labels`** `{ kept?: string; cut?: string; later?: string }`: Column heads. Default In, Cut, Later.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<ScopeCut
  title="The smallest version of lesson-first"
  kept={[
    'Start a lesson with no account',
    'Keep progress in the browser',
    { text: 'Ask for an account after the lesson', note: 'With the progress as the reason' },
  ]}
  cut={['Level test before the first lesson', 'Social sign-in', 'Welcome tour']}
  later={['Move guest progress to a second device']}
/>
```

**Example: The scope of a review**

```mdx
<ScopeCut
  labels={{ kept: 'Looked at', cut: 'Left out' }}
  kept={['Web app, signed out', 'The first session only', 'English interface']}
  cut={['iOS and Android apps', 'Paid plans', 'Anything after day one']}
/>
```

## Claims

`J-06` · Claims sorted by how they are known: measured, observed, reported, assumed.

**Use it for**

- Review, "Where it loses people": what I saw apart from what I guess about other users.
- Experiment, "Context": the evidence that the problem is real, and what is still an assumption.

**Skills Map:** territories cross-cutting, discovery, measurement; skills `evidence-vs-assumptions`, `evidence-strength`, `research-synthesis`, `verification`, `cognitive-biases`, `causal-reasoning`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`claims`** *(required)* `{ text: string; evidence: 'measured' | 'observed' | 'reported' | 'assumed'; source?: string }[]`: In any order. The figure groups them from strongest to weakest.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Claims
  title="What I know about the first session, and how"
  claims={[
    {
      text: '21% of new visitors finish a first lesson',
      evidence: 'measured',
      source: 'Analytics, 28 days',
    },
    {
      text: 'People stop longest at the level question',
      evidence: 'observed',
      source: '5 think-aloud sessions',
    },
    {
      text: 'They want to see a lesson before signing up',
      evidence: 'reported',
      source: '2 of 5 participants',
    },
    {
      text: 'They would create an account after a good lesson',
      evidence: 'assumed',
      source: 'What the experiment tests',
    },
  ]}
  evidence="illustrative"
  source="Example claims"
/>
```

## Quote

`J-07` · Someone's own words, with who said it and in what situation.

**Use it for**

- Interview: the sentence that carries "The decision" or "How they knew".
- A line from a usability session, a support email or a survey answer that shows the problem better than a paraphrase.

**Not for:** Your own conclusions. A quote is reported evidence, not a pull quote of the article.

**Skills Map:** territories discovery, measurement, retention; skills `user-interviews`, `research-synthesis`, `pain-points`, `feedback-analysis`, `usage-observation`, `support-insights`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`text`** *(required)* `string`: The words, without quotation marks.
- **`who`** `string`: Who said it. For users, a description, not a name.
- **`context`** `string`: Where and when.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Quote
  text="I closed it at the sign-up form. I did not know yet if the lessons were any good."
  who="New learner, first session"
  context="Think-aloud session"
  evidence="illustrative"
/>
```

## Verdict

`J-08` · How it ended: what the evidence said and what was done about it.

**Use it for**

- Experiment, "What I learned": the last figure of the entry.
- Improvement, "Effect", when a change was kept or reverted.

**Not for:** Before the result exists. A running experiment shows the Hypothesis, not a pending verdict.

**Skills Map:** territories measurement, cross-cutting; skills `iterate-expand-stop`, `interpreting-results`, `balancing-signals`, `reversible-decisions`, `accountability`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`verdict`** *(required)* `'supported' | 'not-supported' | 'inconclusive' | 'pending'`: The same values as `verdict` in the front matter.
- **`decision`** *(required)* `'keep' | 'iterate' | 'revert' | 'stop' | 'pending'`: The same values as `decision` in the front matter.
- **`reason`** `string`: Why: the number and its uncertainty.
- **`next`** `string`: What happens next.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example**

```mdx
<Verdict
  verdict="supported"
  decision="keep"
  reason="First-lesson completion went from 21.2% to 27.9%. The 95% interval for the difference is +2.9 to +10.4 points. Accounts per visitor held."
  next="Move the account prompt to the end of lesson two and measure who comes back within 7 days."
  evidence="illustrative"
/>
```

**Example: Inconclusive**

```mdx
<Verdict
  verdict="inconclusive"
  decision="iterate"
  reason="The interval for the difference runs from −3.9 to +6.2 points. Two weeks of traffic cannot tell these apart."
/>
```
